A task option reaches a document from the CLI as a markdown task item in the ask's list ('- [x] Hold: Wait for review'); the issue's progress line (dispatch read) is what shows the count a drop would change.

api's TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves refuses this pod's Postgres, whose default collation is byte order, and says so itself. It is the environment, not a failure.
deviations: The weighing of an item keeps the item's own list-item attributes on both sides and removes only checked, rather than comparing with an attribute-less item: label, listType and spread are layout a rebuilt list carries anyway, and comparing without them would refuse an edit for a difference no reader sees - the shape of bug the two rounds before fixed.

callerSentItems was kept and given the caller's own line to charge, rather than deleted in favour of building the sent items from the options again: the budget charge is of the nodes the merge writes, and rebuilding them a second time is the drift the round before removed.
discoveredComplexity: A list item writes one attribute as content, checked, and every other as layout. That is why the weighing of an item cannot be a plain comparison against a fresh item: it has to keep the layout attributes and drop that one.

pmdoc writes a soft break as a hardbreak node carrying isInline, and a line feed a text node ends with as nothing, while pmdoc.TextContent reads both back as a line feed. Any comparison built from TextContent therefore writes a break a person typed as markup their line does not hold.
